text:
We are who we are.
Enough of history and stories!
Let the dead be! Let them bury their dead as God commands.

We do not live from the past,
nor wind up memory.
We are murky and fresh, a water rushing over its source.

We are the being that grows.
We are a straight river.
We are the fearful beat of an unresolved heart.

We are barbarous, simple.
We are, unto death, Iberian,
who have never yet managed to appear pure, whole, and true.

We feed on all that was,
growing as we transform,
and so we are who we are, blow by blow and dead by dead.

To the streets! The hour has come
to walk out in our own skin
and show that, since we live, we announce something new.

I do not deny my origins,
but I say that we shall be
much more than what is known, the forces of a beginning.

Spaniards with a future,
and Spaniards who, because they are so,
though they embody the past, cannot call it good.

I remember our errors
with bitter spite and a fair wind.
Wrath and light, father Spain, I wake you from your sleep.

I say again who you are.
I think of you again, suspended.
I fight again as it matters, and begin where I begin.

I will not justify you
as a pettifogging lawyer would;
I would be a poet and write your first verse.

My Spain, struggle
that torments my inmost self,
to save myself and save you, I spell you out with love.

translation.title: Spain on the March
